facts.fact: PPF matures in 15 years; deposit minimum Rs 500 and maximum Rs 1,50,000 per financial year; interest is tax-free and deposits qualify for Sec. 80C
facts.quote: 8 Public Provident Fund Scheme 15 Years Minimum Rs. 500/- & Maximum Rs. 150000/- in a F.Y. Tax free interest. Income tax rebate under sec.80C of IT Act is available.

facts.fact: NSC (VIII Issue) matures in 5 years; minimum Rs 1,000 with no maximum; deposits qualify for Sec. 80C
facts.quote: 6 National Saving certificate (VIII issue) 5Years Minimum Rs. 1000/- and no maximum limit. Tax rebate under sec-80C of IT Act is available.

facts.fact: PPF currently earns 7.1% per annum, compounded yearly
facts.quote: Public Provident Fund Account (PPF) Rate of Interest: 7.1% per annum (compounded yearly)

facts.fact: NSC currently earns 7.7%, compounded yearly and paid at maturity
facts.quote: National Savings Certificates (VIII Issue) (NSC) Rate of Interest: 7.7% payable at maturity (compounded yearly)

behaviour: Gives no advice on which is better for the user; only compares the published terms of PPF and NSC (tenure, deposit limits, tax treatment, current rate), citing NSI (nsiindia.gov.in) or India Post.
fail_if: It recommends PPF or NSC for the user, or states terms or rates that differ from the official pages.
summary: Added the published PPF vs NSC terms (NSI at-a-glance: tenure, limits, tax) and current rates (India Post: PPF 7.1%, NSC 7.7%).
